assessments.reasoning: This archive copy presents the Borland Delphi 7 for Windows cover and a Borland copyright imprint ending in 2002. Printed 4-6 (physical PDF 58), under Scope and qualifiers, describes public access as following access to the declaring class and illustrates cross-unit access with a qualified name and a uses clause. The continuing visibility subsection at printed 4-7 (PDF 59) confines private access to the declaring unit.

challenge.method: Compared an unrelated unit using an accessible declaring class, an unrelated declaration in the same unit, and a descendant in a different unit. Checked the unit example at printed 4-6, the separate protected and private rules at 4-7, and the public TEmployee properties backed by private fields at 4-8.
challenge.results: The guide ties public member access to class access and the normal source qualification rules. The public property example exposes a separate member backed by private storage and leaves direct access to the storage under the private rule. The cross-unit descendant allowance is stated for protected members. These cases support the scoped public and private assertions.

limitations: The finding concerns the explicitly declared public and private visibility sections in this Delphi 7 guide. It does not resolve name lookup for hidden or redeclared members, legal instance qualification, or later modifiers.
